svg.title: Issue 001 Page 3 Neighborhood Watch
svg.text: THREE CORRIDORS,
NO SINGLE STORY
Reports of damaged locks and coordinated movement overlap. The witnesses do not. The Underground Press
compared their accounts without turning resemblance into certainty. Three below-street approaches appear
repeatedly in the reports collected for Issue 001: a waterfront service door, the green-lamp approach,
and a delivery turn used after closing. The descriptions overlap at the edges-dark clothing, quick
movement, little conversation-but none supplies a clear face, name, or shared destination. A shopkeeper
near the waterfront said a rear latch was bent inward sometime after the last delivery. The shopkeeper
heard two sets of steps and later found three muddy marks. "That does not make three people," the
shopkeeper said. "It makes three marks." Nothing was reported missing. At the green-lamp approach, a cart
puller saw "four shadows moving like they had practiced." Fog and a low lamp shortened the view. The
puller could not say whether the figures entered a restricted passage or simply crossed in front of it. A
second neighbor at the same approach heard only one runner. The delivery-turn report is stranger and less
complete. A folded strip of dark cloth was found caught on a screw beside a recently repaired lock. The
material is common work cloth. It bears no insignia. Two residents independently used the name "Foot
Clan" after hearing about it; neither claimed direct knowledge. The newsroom has not confirmed that such
a group caused these incidents-or that the name identifies a real organization at all. What can be said
is narrower. Several neighbors changed closing routines. Volunteer latch checks found ordinary wear as
well as deliberate-looking damage, and the difference was not always obvious. Late delivery riders report
more paired travel. The Crust Bucket's unusual midnight orders occurred near the same broad set of
passages, but an order pattern is not an identification. The desk will continue comparing times,
descriptions, and physical traces. For now, neighbors should record what they directly saw or heard,
distinguish it from what somebody else repeated, and avoid following unidentified people into restricted
corridors. Suspicion is not a public service unless it stays honest about its limits.
WE'RE ALL LOOKING FOR A PLACE TO LAND.
